question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Writing habit is a good and easily exercise for the brain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. good and easily exercise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Exercise” is a noun here, and a noun must be modified by an adjective, never by an adverb.

◦ “Easily” is an adverb (सरलता से); the adjective form is easy (आसान). Since “good” (adjective) and the second word are joined by “and”, both must belong to the same class.

◦ Correct: Writing habit is a good and easy exercise for the brain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “for the brain.” is correct — preposition “for” + noun phrase.

• Option 3 “Writing habit is a” is correct — singular subject with singular verb “is” and article “a”.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the adverb “easily” is clearly misused for the adjective “easy”.

NOTE

• Adjective modifies a noun; adverb modifies a verb/adjective/adverb: “He is a quick learner” but “He learns quickly”.

• Frequently tested adjective–adverb pairs: easy/easily, hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Most impressive / was record breaking / 75.6 FPS on Crysis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was record breaking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase needs the indefinite article “a” before the singular countable noun phrase “record-breaking 75.6 FPS”, and “record-breaking” must work as a single compound adjective.

◦ An article is compulsory before a singular countable noun that is being mentioned for the first time. (अनिश्चित उपपद)

◦ Correct: Most impressive was a record-breaking 75.6 FPS on Crysis.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “75.6 FPS on Crysis.” is fine — the figure with the preposition “on” and the game’s name is correctly used.

• Option 2 “Most impressive” is a correct fronted complement of the sentence.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the article is missing in segment 3.

NOTE

• Compound adjectives placed before a noun are hyphenated: record-breaking performance, well-known author, ten-year-old boy.

• Numbers/measurements still take an article when used as a countable noun: “a 40% rise”, “an 8-hour shift”.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Instead of the sweet taste she expected, it was ______ - like alum
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bitter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bitter means having a sharp, unpleasant taste, the opposite of sweet. (कड़वा)

◦ The sentence sets up a contrast with “Instead of the sweet taste she expected”, so the blank must carry the sense opposite to “sweet”.

◦ Alum (फिटकरी) is famously astringent and bitter, which confirms the choice.

◦ Correct: Instead of the sweet taste she expected, it was bitter - like alum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dulcet — sweet and soothing, usually of sound (मधुर); it would repeat, not contrast with, “sweet”.

• Aromatic — having a pleasant, distinctive smell (सुगंधित); it describes smell, not the contrast in taste.

• Tenacious — holding on firmly, persistent (दृढ़); unrelated to taste.

NOTE

• Taste vocabulary for SSC: sour (खट्टा), pungent (तीखा), bland/insipid (फीका), savoury (नमकीन), acrid (कड़वा-तीखा).

• Contrast markers such as “instead of”, “rather than”, “on the contrary” signal that an opposite word fits the blank.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

What should I doing if the power goes out?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. should I do.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A modal auxiliary (should, would, can, may, must) is always followed by the bare infinitive (V1), never by V-ing or V3. (सहायक क्रिया के बाद मूल क्रिया)

◦ In an interrogative sentence the pattern is: Wh-word + modal + subject + V1 → “What should I do…?”

◦ The “if” clause is in the simple present (“goes out”), which suits a first-conditional style question about the future.

◦ Correct: What should I do if the power goes out?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “shall I does” is wrong — a modal can never take “does”, and “shall” with “I” would change the sense to an offer.

• Option 2 “No improvement” is wrong because “should I doing” is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 “should I had done” is wrong — the correct perfect modal form would be “should I have done”, which also changes the tense wrongly.

NOTE

• Modal + V1: “She can swim”, “He must go”, “You may leave”.

• Modal + have + V3 expresses past speculation/regret: “I should have gone”, “She must have forgotten”.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

He is interested in how our (perceptions) of death affect the way we live.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. approaches.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Perception means the way in which something is regarded, understood or interpreted. (धारणा, दृष्टिकोण)

◦ Approach here carries the sense of a particular way of viewing or dealing with something, which is the closest available match for “ways of regarding death”.

◦ Correct: He is interested in how our approaches to death affect the way we live.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ignorance — lack of knowledge (अज्ञानता); it is the absence of understanding, not a way of understanding.

• Bewilderment — a state of confusion (घबराहट); it names an emotion, not a viewpoint.

• Misconception — a wrong or mistaken idea (भ्रांति); “perception” is neutral and need not be wrong.

NOTE

• Closer one-word synonyms of perception: outlook, viewpoint, notion, impression, understanding.

• Remember the pair: perception (धारणा) vs deception (धोखा) vs conception (कल्पना/धारणा का बनना).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The room beneath the collapsed building was empty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. mended.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Collapsed means fallen down or caved in suddenly. (ढह गया)

◦ Mended means repaired or put back into good condition (मरम्मत किया हुआ), which is the direct opposite of a structure that has fallen apart.

◦ Correct: The opposite of a collapsed building is a mended (repaired) building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Finished — completed or ended (समाप्त); it refers to completion, not to repair, so it is not an antonym.

• Cracked — split or broken (चटका हुआ); this is a synonym-side word, close in sense to collapsed.

• Choked — blocked or unable to breathe (अवरुद्ध); unrelated to a building’s structural state.

NOTE

• Synonyms of collapse: crumble, cave in, give way, disintegrate, topple.

• Antonyms of collapse: build, erect, construct, strengthen, restore.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

I began with writing one a week and now I do so every day.
option_3: now I do so every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. one a week and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the adverb of frequency “once”, not the numeral “one”. “Once a week” means one time in a week. (सप्ताह में एक बार)

◦ Frequency is expressed as: once a week, twice a month, thrice a year, and it contrasts naturally with “every day” later in the sentence.

◦ Correct: I began with writing once a week and now I do so every day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “I began with writing” is acceptable — “begin with” + gerund shows the starting point of a habit.

• Option 3 “now I do so every day.” is correct — “do so” substitutes for the earlier verb phrase.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because “one a week” must be “once a week”.

NOTE

• Numeral vs frequency adverb: one → once, two → twice, three → thrice/three times.

• After “begin/start”, both gerund and infinitive are possible: “She began singing” = “She began to sing”.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

They will took their grandchildren to the zoo.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. took their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Will” is a modal and must be followed by the bare infinitive (V1), so “will took” (modal + V2) is ungrammatical.

◦ Among the given choices, the only grammatically complete verb phrase is the simple past “took”, which fits a completed action. (भूतकाल)

◦ Correct: They took their grandchildren to the zoo.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “No improvement” is wrong because “will took” breaks the modal + V1 rule.

• Option 2 “taken their” is wrong — “taken” (V3) needs an auxiliary such as “have/had/were” before it.

• Option 3 “takes their” is wrong — the plural subject “They” takes the base verb “take”, not “takes”.

NOTE

• Verb forms of take: take – took – taken; of go: go – went – gone; of write: write – wrote – written.

• Modal + V1 always: “will go”, “can do”, “must see”; never “will went”, “can did”.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Curious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Uninterested.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Curious means eager to know or learn something; inquisitive. (जिज्ञासु)

◦ Uninterested means not interested, showing no eagerness to know (उदासीन), which is the exact opposite of curiosity.

◦ Correct: A curious student asks questions, whereas an uninterested student asks none.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Passionate — showing strong feeling or enthusiasm (उत्साही); it is closer in spirit to curious, not opposite.

• Doubtful — uncertain, having doubts (संदेहपूर्ण); doubt is not the opposite of curiosity.

• Complex — complicated, having many parts (जटिल); it describes things, not attitude.

NOTE

• Synonyms of curious: inquisitive, prying, interested, questioning, nosy.

• Do not confuse uninterested (not interested) with disinterested (impartial, unbiased) — a very common SSC trap.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

When we reached my room, I couldn’t ______ back my smile.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb “hold back” means to restrain or suppress an emotion. (रोकना, दबाना)

◦ “Couldn’t” is a modal (could + not), and a modal is always followed by the bare infinitive V1, so only “hold” can follow.

◦ Correct: When we reached my room, I couldn’t hold back my smile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “squeeze” is V1 but “squeeze back” is not an idiomatic phrasal verb for suppressing a smile.

• Option 3 “held” is the past form (V2) and cannot follow the modal “couldn’t”.

• Option 4 “kept” is also V2, and “keep back a smile” is not the standard collocation.

NOTE

• Common “hold” phrasal verbs: hold back (restrain), hold on (wait), hold up (delay/rob), hold out (resist).

• Emotions collocate with: hold back tears, choke back sobs, fight back tears, suppress a laugh.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

They were ______ there when Janvi heard something large and heavy collide with the door.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. almost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Almost is an adverb meaning “nearly, very close to but not completely”. (लगभग)

◦ “They were almost there” is a fixed, idiomatic expression meaning they had nearly reached the destination, which suits the sudden interruption described.

◦ Correct: They were almost there when Janvi heard something large and heavy collide with the door.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Much is used with uncountable nouns or comparatives (“much better”), not before “there”.

• Most is a superlative/quantifier (“most people”, “most beautiful”) and does not fit an adverb slot before “there”.

• About can mean “approximately”, but it precedes numbers or quantities (“about ten minutes”), not the adverb “there”.

NOTE

• Almost + there/all/everyone/never: “almost every day”, “almost never”.

• Distinguish almost (nearly) from mostly (mainly) and at most (maximum).

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anarcy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is ANARCHY, with the letters c-h-y at the end; the option drops the “h”.

◦ Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority or government. (अराजकता)

◦ Correct: The country slipped into complete anarchy after the coup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Adverse (प्रतिकूल) — unfavourable or harmful; correctly spelt.

• Annul (रद्द करना) — to declare invalid, especially a marriage or law; correctly spelt with double “n”.

• Adulterate (मिलावट करना) — to make impure by adding an inferior substance; correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words from Greek “arche” (rule): anarchy, monarchy, oligarchy, hierarchy — all keep -archy.

• Do not confuse adverse (unfavourable) with averse (unwilling, opposed to).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

For better or (for) worse
option_4: To accept whatever results; good or bad
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To accept whatever results; good or bad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “for better or (for) worse” means whatever the consequences may be — good or bad — one accepts the situation. (जो भी परिणाम हो, अच्छा या बुरा)

◦ It comes from the traditional marriage vow “for better, for worse”, indicating unconditional acceptance.

◦ Correct: For better or for worse, we have decided to shift to a new city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• “Become out of control” is expressed by idioms like get out of hand or run riot.

• “Extreme enthusiasm” matches gung-ho or full of beans.

• “To be in trouble” matches in hot water or in a fix.

NOTE

• Related idioms: come what may (whatever happens), take the rough with the smooth, through thick and thin (in all circumstances).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Disappointed and annoyed about something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disgruntled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disgruntled means angry, dissatisfied or discontented, especially because one’s expectations were not met. (असंतुष्ट, नाराज़)

◦ It combines exactly the two ideas in the clue — disappointment and annoyance.

◦ Correct: The disgruntled employees refused to attend the meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Contented (संतुष्ट) — happy and satisfied; it is the opposite of the required meaning.

• Dissuade (मना करना) — to persuade someone not to do something; it is a verb, not an adjective describing mood.

• Surreal (अवास्तविक) — strange and dreamlike, unreal; unrelated to emotion of annoyance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of disgruntled: aggrieved, resentful, discontented, peeved, sulky.

• Antonyms: pleased, satisfied, gratified, contented.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

To move about from place to place aimlessly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Meander.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meander means to wander aimlessly, or (of a river) to follow a winding course. (लक्ष्यहीन घूमना, टेढ़ा-मेढ़ा बहना)

◦ The key idea in the clue is aimless movement, which only “meander” conveys.

◦ Correct: We spent the afternoon meandering through the narrow lanes of the old city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Meadow (चारागाह) — a field of grass, a noun denoting a place, not an action.

• Path (रास्ता) — a track or way; again a noun, and it implies a fixed route, not aimlessness.

• Stream (धारा) — a small river; it names a water body rather than aimless movement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of meander: ramble, roam, wander, saunter, stroll, drift.

• Note the geography use too: a meander is a bend in a river; an abandoned meander forms an oxbow lake.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Long in the tooth
option_1: The show has come to an end
option_2: Be optimistic, even difficult times will lead to better days
option_3: To be old, often too old to do something
option_4: Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be old, often too old to do something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “long in the tooth” means rather old, past one’s prime. (बूढ़ा होना)

◦ It comes from horse-trading: a horse’s gums recede with age, so its teeth appear longer — hence age is judged by the teeth.

◦ Correct: He is a bit long in the tooth to be playing professional cricket now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• “The show has come to an end” corresponds to the curtain falls or that’s all she wrote.

• “Be optimistic, even difficult times will lead to better days” corresponds to every cloud has a silver lining.

• “Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale” is the word genocide, not an idiom.

NOTE

• Other age idioms: over the hill (past one’s best), no spring chicken (not young), getting on in years.

• Related horse idiom: don’t look a gift horse in the mouth — do not question the value of a gift.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

“What ______ your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. does.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a simple present interrogative asking about a habitual activity (a job), so the auxiliary do/does is needed with the main verb “do”.

◦ The subject “your dad” is third person singular, and in the simple present the singular subject takes does. (एकवचन कर्ता के साथ does)

◦ Correct: “What does your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?”

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “is” is wrong — “is … do” is impossible; “is doing” would be needed, which changes the structure.

• Option 2 “have” is wrong — the perfect tense would require “has done”, not “have … do”.

• Option 4 “do” is wrong — “do” is used with I/we/you/they and plural subjects, not with a singular subject like “your dad”.

NOTE

• Simple present question pattern: Wh-word + do/does + subject + V1.

• Once “does/did” is used, the main verb stays in the base form: “What did he say?”, not “What did he said?”.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Advocate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Advocate (verb) means to publicly recommend or support a particular cause or policy; as a noun it means a person who pleads for a cause. (समर्थन करना; वकील)

◦ “Support” carries the same core sense of backing or speaking in favour of something.

◦ Correct: Many scientists advocate (= support) stricter limits on carbon emissions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Justice (न्याय) — fairness or the legal system; it is related to the courtroom sense but is not a synonym of the word itself.

• Forever (हमेशा के लिए) — an adverb of time; completely unrelated in meaning.

• Experience (अनुभव) — knowledge gained through practice; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of advocate: champion, endorse, uphold, promote, back, espouse.

• Antonyms of advocate: oppose, resist, discourage, denounce, impugn.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

(The people of Philippines has voted) to elect a new president.
option_2: The people of Philippines have voted
option_3: The people of the Philippines have voted
option_4: The people of the Philippines has voted
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The people of the Philippines have voted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed together. First, the definite article “the” is compulsory before the names of countries that are plural in form or a group of islands: the Philippines, the Netherlands, the Maldives, the USA.

◦ Second, the noun “people” in the sense of “persons” is plural, so it takes the plural verb have, not “has”. (लोग — बहुवचन)

◦ Correct: The people of the Philippines have voted to elect a new president.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the printed segment has two errors — a missing article and a wrong verb.

• Option 2 fixes the verb but still omits “the” before Philippines.

• Option 4 supplies the article but keeps the singular verb “has”, which does not agree with “people”.

NOTE

• “The” with countries: the Philippines, the Netherlands, the UAE, the UK; but no article with India, China, Japan.

• “People” = persons (plural verb); “peoples” = communities/nations, as in “the peoples of Asia”.

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PRESENCE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PRESENCE is spelt correctly — p-r-e-s-e-n-c-e. It means the state of being present or a person’s bearing. (उपस्थिति)

◦ Correct: Your presence at the meeting is mandatory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “CAMOFLAGUE” is wrong; the correct spelling is CAMOUFLAGE (छद्मावरण) — hiding by blending with the surroundings.

• Option 2 “COMPARSION” is wrong; the correct spelling is COMPARISON (तुलना), formed from “compare” + “-ison”.

• Option 3 “GUAGE” is wrong; the correct spelling is GAUGE (मापक) — to measure, or an instrument for measuring.

NOTE

• Note the noun–adjective pair: presence → present; absence → absent.

• Other commonly misspelt SSC words: occurrence, maintenance, embarrass, harass, questionnaire, liaison.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. transmits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Transmit means to pass on, send or communicate something from one person or place to another. (संप्रेषित करना)

◦ The subject “Body language” is singular, so the singular present verb transmits is required, and the object “ideas or thoughts” shows that communication is meant.

◦ Correct: Body language transmits ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Delimit — to fix the limits or boundaries of something (परिसीमन करना); it does not mean to convey.

• Intermit — to stop or suspend temporarily; it is rare and gives the opposite idea of continuous conveying.

• Retransmit — to transmit again; nothing in the passage suggests repetition of an earlier message.

NOTE

• Words from Latin “mittere” (to send): transmit, emit, submit, admit, remit, omit.

• Collocations: transmit a signal/disease/message/knowledge.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wink.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A wink is the closing and opening of one eye quickly, used as a private signal. (आँख मारना)

◦ The passage says the gesture “can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking” — both are classic functions of a wink.

◦ Correct: A wink can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nod — to move the head up and down; it signals agreement, and the passage assigns approval to blank 3.

• Shake — a side-to-side head movement signalling refusal, which the passage assigns to blank 4.

• Clap — striking the palms together to applaud; it expresses appreciation, not flirtation or joking.

NOTE

• Gesture vocabulary: shrug (indifference), beckon (call closer), wave (greeting/farewell), frown (displeasure).

• Idiom: a nod is as good as a wink — a hint is enough for someone who understands.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. nod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A nod is a short up-and-down movement of the head that universally signals yes, agreement or approval. (सिर हिलाकर सहमति देना)

◦ The blank is followed by “signifies approval”, and it is contrasted with the next blank, which “indicates a negative reaction”.

◦ Correct: A nod signifies approval, while a shake of the head indicates a negative reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shake (of the head) conveys disapproval or refusal — that is the contrast word needed in blank 4, not here.

• Wink conveys flirtation or a shared joke and has already been used in blank 2.

• Clap shows applause or appreciation, which is not the same as signifying approval of a statement.

NOTE

• Useful phrases: nod off (fall asleep), give the nod (approve/select), on the nod (approved without discussion).

• Contrast pairs in cloze passages are signalled by connectors such as while, whereas, but, on the other hand.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. shake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A shake of the head is a side-to-side movement that signals no, refusal or disapproval. (सिर हिलाकर मना करना)

◦ The blank is immediately followed by “of the head indicates a negative reaction”, and the connector “while” demands a contrast with the approving “nod” in blank 3.

◦ Correct: A nod signifies approval, while a shake of the head indicates a negative reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Clap — applause with the hands; one does not “clap of the head”, so it fails the collocation test.

• Wink — an eye gesture already used for flirting/joking in blank 2.

• Nod — signals approval, the positive gesture used in blank 3, hence the opposite of what is needed.

NOTE

• Collocation clue: only nod and shake combine with “of the head”; the phrase after the blank often decides the answer in cloze tests.

• Related expressions: shake hands (greet), shake off (get rid of), shake up (reorganise/shock).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Body language (1) ______ ideas or thoughts by certain actions, either intentionally or unintentionally. A (2) ______ can be a way of flirting or indicating that the party is only joking . A (3) ______ signifies approval, while (4) ______ of the head indicates a negative reaction. Other forms of non (5) ______ language can be found in Braille (a system of raised dots read with the fingertips), signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals..

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. linguistic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Linguistic means relating to language or words, so non-linguistic language means communication that does not use spoken or written words. (भाषा-संबंधी)

◦ The examples given — Braille, signal flags, Morse code and smoke signals — are all systems of communication without ordinary speech, which fixes the word after “non”.

◦ Correct: Other forms of non linguistic language can be found in Braille, signal flags, Morse code, and smoke signals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Holistic — dealing with the whole rather than the parts (समग्र); it does not contrast with words.

• Logistic — relating to the organisation and movement of resources (रसद-संबंधी); irrelevant here.

• Parodistic — relating to parody or humorous imitation; it does not describe a mode of communication.

NOTE

• Related terms: verbal (using words) vs non-verbal communication; paralinguistic features are tone, pitch and pauses.

• Braille was devised by Louis Braille (France, 1824); Morse code is named after Samuel Morse.

question: Which of the following features distinguishes the Elephanta Caves from other rock-cut sites of early India?
option_1: They are primarily Buddhist caves with large stupas.
option_2: The caves focus on Shaivite themes and feature sculptural depth through light and shadow.
option_3: They contain a mix of Jain and Vaishnavite depictions in pillar halls.
option_4: The caves are entirely monolithic structures from the Mauryan period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The caves focus on Shaivite themes and feature sculptural depth through light and shadow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Elephanta Caves (एलीफेंटा गुफाएं) are located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri) in Mumbai Harbour, Maharashtra.

• They are predominantly Shaivite (dedicated to Lord Shiva), famous for the colossal Trimurti Sadashiva sculpture that uses light and shadow to give great sculptural depth.

• The caves were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The caves are dated mainly to the Kalachuri/early medieval period (c. 5th–8th century CE).

• The main Cave 1 contains iconic panels like Nataraja, Ardhanarishvara and Gangadhara.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

NOTE

• They are primarily Buddhist caves with large stupas (Option 1): Describes Buddhist chaitya sites like Ajanta or Karla, not Elephanta.

• They contain a mix of Jain and Vaishnavite depictions in pillar halls (Option 3): Not characteristic of Elephanta, which is essentially Shaivite.

• The caves are entirely monolithic structures from the Mauryan period (Option 4): Incorrect; Elephanta is rock-cut but not Mauryan, and monolithic temples are seen at Mahabalipuram/Ellora.

question:
Read the statements about the Goncha Festival of Bastar:
1.) Tupki, a mock gun made of bamboo, uses Goncha fruit as bullets.
2.) The chariot procession was started by Chalukya rulers.
3.) Rath Yatra begins on Ashadh Shukla Dashmi and ends on Dutiya.
Which of the above statements are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Goncha Festival (गोंचा उत्सव) is a traditional festival of Bastar, Chhattisgarh, associated with the Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath.

• Tupki, a mock gun made of bamboo, uses the small green Goncha (Malkangni) fruit as bullets — statement 1 is correct.

• The chariot/Rath tradition here is traced to the Chalukya (Kakatiya-Chalukya) rulers of Bastar — statement 2 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Statement 3 gives the wrong tithi sequence for the Rath Yatra, so it is not counted as correct.

• Bastar is also famous for the world's longest festival, Bastar Dussehra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 2): Excludes correct statement 1 and includes wrong statement 3.

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 3): Includes wrong statement 3.

• 1, 2 and 3 are correct (Option 4): Wrong because statement 3 is incorrect.

question:
Fill in the blanks:
In Carnatic music, a laghu with five beats is known as ___ jaati.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khanda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Carnatic music (कर्नाटक संगीत), the laghu (लघु) can take different numbers of beats depending on its jaati.

• A laghu of five beats corresponds to the Khanda jaati (खंड जाति).

• The five jaatis and their laghu counts are: Tishra-3, Chaturashra-4, Khanda-5, Mishra-7, Sankeerna-9.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tala in Carnatic music is built from three angas: laghu, dhrutam and anudhrutam.

• The Suladi Sapta Tala system uses these seven basic talas with the five jaatis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Tishra (Option 1): Laghu of 3 beats.

• Chaturashra (Option 2): Laghu of 4 beats.

• Mishra (Option 4): Laghu of 7 beats.

question: Which of the following statements about Judo is correct?
option_1: Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan.
option_2: India's first National Judo Championship was held in 1970 at Delhi University.
option_3: Kalpana Devi won gold at the 2010 Judo World Cup.
option_4: Judo became an Olympic sport in 1965.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Judo (जूडो) was founded in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan, developing it from traditional jujutsu.

• Kano established the Kodokan institute, the headquarters of Judo.

• Judo emphasises throws (nage-waza) and grappling (katame-waza).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Judo made its Olympic debut in 1964 at the Tokyo Games (men); women's judo was added in 1992.

• The governing body is the International Judo Federation (IJF).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• India's first National Judo Championship was held in 1970 at Delhi University (Option 2): An incorrect factual claim used as a distractor.

• Kalpana Devi won gold at the 2010 Judo World Cup (Option 3): Incorrect; not a factual achievement of hers.

• Judo became an Olympic sport in 1965 (Option 4): Wrong year — it entered the Olympics in 1964, not 1965.

question: Where and when will the 59th National Cross Country Championships – 2025 be held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12th January 2025, Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 59th National Cross Country Championships (59वीं राष्ट्रीय क्रॉस कंट्री चैंपियनशिप) were held on 12 January 2025 at Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.

• The event is organised by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).

• The Services and Railways teams dominated the championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Cross country running is an endurance discipline run over natural, open-country terrain.

• The AFI is the apex body governing athletics in India, affiliated to World Athletics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

NOTE

• 10th January 2025, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Wrong date and venue.

• 15th January 2025, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Wrong date and venue.

• 12th January 2025, Jaipur, Rajasthan (Option 4): Correct date but wrong venue/state.

question: What is the core structural focus of the 2024 India–UAE Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) within India's international investment strategy?
option_1: Proposes joint sovereign funds and links INR swap with UAE banks.
option_2: Focuses on pre-establishment rights and UAE-based arbitration.
option_3: Assures post-establishment investor confidence via standard and national treatment.
option_4: Aims at GCC-wide tax regulation under India-led digital framework.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assures post-establishment investor confidence via standard and national treatment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The India–UAE Bilateral Investment Treaty (भारत-यूएई द्विपक्षीय निवेश संधि) signed in 2024 follows India's 2016 Model BIT framework.

• Its core focus is post-establishment protection, assuring investors of fair treatment, national treatment and non-discrimination after investment is made.

• It deliberately excludes pre-establishment (market access) commitments, reflecting India's cautious model.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's Model BIT emphasises an exhaustion of local remedies requirement before international arbitration.

• The UAE is among India's top trade partners; the India-UAE CEPA came into force in 2022.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Proposes joint sovereign funds and links INR swap with UAE banks (Option 1): Not the structural focus of the BIT.

• Focuses on pre-establishment rights and UAE-based arbitration (Option 2): India's model avoids pre-establishment rights.

• Aims at GCC-wide tax regulation under India-led digital framework (Option 4): A BIT deals with investment protection, not GCC-wide taxation.

question:
Fill in the blanks:
The Santosh Trophy 2022–23 final was uniquely held in _____, where Karnataka defeated Meghalaya to win the title after 54 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Riyadh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Santosh Trophy 2022–23 (संतोष ट्रॉफी) final was uniquely held outside India, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (रियाद).

• Karnataka defeated Meghalaya in the final to win the title after 54 years (their previous win was in 1969).

• The Santosh Trophy is the premier state-level football competition in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• It is named after Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury, Maharaja of Santosh (in present-day Bangladesh).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

NOTE

• Dubai (Option 1): A city in the UAE; did not host this final.

• Doha (Option 3): Capital of Qatar; not the venue.

• Muscat (Option 4): Capital of Oman; not the venue.

question: Which of the following statements best captures the essence of "Landscapes of Loss: The Story of an Indian Drought" by Kavitha Iyer?
option_1: A study on drought's human and ecological impacts in India.
option_2: A fictional story about a family in a drought-hit area.
option_3: A history of monsoon patterns and ancient agriculture in India.
option_4: A colonial-era policy analysis of water management.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A study on drought's human and ecological impacts in India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Landscapes of Loss: The Story of an Indian Drought" is a non-fiction work by journalist Kavitha Iyer.

• It documents the human and ecological impact of recurring drought (सूखा), focusing on the Marathwada region of Maharashtra.

• It examines agrarian distress, migration and water scarcity through real reportage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The book highlights issues such as farmer suicides and sugarcane cultivation in drought-prone areas.

• It is a work of reportage-based non-fiction, not a novel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• A fictional story about a family in a drought-hit area (Option 2): Wrong; the book is non-fiction reportage, not fiction.

• A history of monsoon patterns and ancient agriculture in India (Option 3): Not the theme of the book.

• A colonial-era policy analysis of water management (Option 4): The book deals with contemporary drought, not colonial policy.

question:
Consider the following statements about glacial landforms:
Statement 1: Hanging valleys are often found opening into main glacial valleys at higher elevations.
Statement 2: Spurs of such hanging valleys are frequently truncated into triangular facets.
Which of the following Statements is/are Correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A hanging valley (लटकती घाटी) is a tributary glacial valley that opens into a deeper main glacial (U-shaped) valley at a higher elevation, often forming a waterfall — Statement 1 is correct.

• The spurs (projecting ridges) of such valleys are eroded and cut off by the glacier into triangular truncated spurs (facets) — Statement 2 is correct.

• Both are classic features of glacial erosion (हिमनदीय अपरदन).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other glacial erosional landforms include cirques, aretes, horns, U-shaped valleys and fjords.

• Depositional landforms include moraines, drumlins, eskers and outwash plains.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Only 1 (Option 1): Incomplete; Statement 2 is also correct.

• Only 2 (Option 2): Incomplete; Statement 1 is also correct.

• Neither 1 nor 2 are correct (Option 4): Wrong, as both statements are true.

question: What is the primary function of the Crew Escape System (CES) on ISRO's Human Rated LVM3 (HLVM3) rocket?
option_1: To guide the crew module into its designated Low Earth Orbit.
option_2: To eject the crew module to safety during launch emergencies.
option_3: To assist in docking the crew module with a space station.
option_4: To provide thermal shielding during re-entry into Earth's atmosphere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To eject the crew module to safety during launch emergencies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Crew Escape System (क्रू एस्केप सिस्टम) is a safety mechanism on ISRO's human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) used in the Gaganyaan mission.

• Its primary function is to quickly pull the crew module away to safety in case of an emergency on the launch pad or during ascent.

• It uses a set of quick-acting solid motors to separate the crew from the malfunctioning rocket.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The CES was successfully demonstrated in the TV-D1 (Test Vehicle Abort Mission-1) in October 2023.

• Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight programme, aiming to send astronauts to Low Earth Orbit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

NOTE

• To guide the crew module into its designated Low Earth Orbit (Option 1): That is the job of the launch vehicle's stages, not the escape system.

• To assist in docking the crew module with a space station (Option 3): Docking is handled by separate docking systems.

• To provide thermal shielding during re-entry into Earth's atmosphere (Option 4): Re-entry heating is handled by the heat shield, not the CES.

question:
Which of the following statements about Justice Sanjiv Khanna is/are true?
1. He is the 51st Chief Justice of India
2. He succeeded Justice D.Y. Chandrachud
3. He served as CJI from 2023
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Justice Sanjiv Khanna (न्यायमूर्ति संजीव खन्ना) is the 51st Chief Justice of India (CJI) — statement 1 is correct.

• He succeeded Justice D.Y. Chandrachud — statement 2 is correct.

• He assumed office as CJI on 11 November 2024, not in 2023, so statement 3 is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Justice Sanjiv Khanna was elevated to the Supreme Court in January 2019.

• The CJI is appointed by the President of India under Article 124 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Includes wrong statement 3 (2023).

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Includes wrong statement 3.

• 1, 2, and 3 all are true (Option 4): Wrong, because statement 3 is false.

question:
Which of the following objectives are part of the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000?
1. Providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age
2. Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend
3. Reducing infant mortality rate below 30 per 1000 live births
4. Promoting delayed marriage for girls
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Population Policy (राष्ट्रीय जनसंख्या नीति) 2000 aimed at making school education free and compulsory up to age 14 (objective 1) — correct.

• It sought to reduce the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) to below 30 per 1000 live births (objective 3) — correct.

• It promoted delayed marriage for girls and raising the age of marriage (objective 4) — correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The immediate objective of NPP 2000 was to address unmet needs for contraception, health infrastructure and personnel.

• Its long-term objective was to achieve a stable population by 2045, consistent with sustainable development.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Objective 2, increasing the fertility rate, is wrong — the policy aimed to *reduce* the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) to replacement level.

• Only 1 and 2 are correct (Option 1): Includes wrong objective 2 and omits 3 and 4.

• Only 1 and 3 are correct (Option 2): Omits correct objective 4.

• 1,2,3 and 4 all are correct (Option 4): Wrong because objective 2 is incorrect.

question: Which pathway in cellular respiration generates the most ATP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electron transport chain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Electron Transport Chain (इलेक्ट्रॉन परिवहन श्रृंखला) is the final stage of aerobic cellular respiration, located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

• It generates the maximum ATP (about 34 out of ~36–38 total) through oxidative phosphorylation.

• It uses electrons carried by NADH and FADH2 and oxygen as the final electron acceptor.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Glycolysis yields a net of 2 ATP, and the Krebs cycle yields 2 ATP (plus electron carriers).

• The enzyme that finally synthesises ATP is ATP synthase, driven by a proton gradient (chemiosmosis).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Glycolysis (Option 1): Occurs in the cytoplasm; nets only 2 ATP per glucose.

• Krebs cycle (Option 2): Occurs in the mitochondrial matrix; directly yields only 2 ATP.

• Fermentation (Option 4): Anaerobic process yielding just 2 ATP, without the electron transport chain.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
a. Eastern Zonal Council meeting 2022
b. States Reorganisation Act passed
c. First Central Zonal Council meeting
solution_text:
The correct answer is b-c-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The States Reorganisation Act (राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम) was passed in 1956, and it created the Zonal Councils — so (b) comes first.

• The Zonal Councils were set up under this Act, hence the First Central Zonal Council meeting (c) followed afterwards.

• The Eastern Zonal Council meeting of 2022 (a) is the most recent event, so the order is b-c-a.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• There are five Zonal Councils (Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, Central) created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

• The Zonal Councils are statutory bodies, chaired by the Union Home Minister.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• c-b-a (Option 2): Wrong; the Act (b) predates the first council meeting (c).

• a-b-c (Option 3): Wrong; places the 2022 event first.

• b-a-c (Option 4): Wrong; places the 2022 event before the first council meeting.

question: Which of the following most accurately describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
option_2: It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
option_3: It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
option_4: It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Right to Property (संपत्ति का अधिकार) was made a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

• It states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law — i.e., deprivation is permitted only through a valid law.

• It is no longer a Fundamental Right (it was removed from Part III).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Earlier, the right to property was a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, both repealed by the 44th Amendment.

• Since it is not a Fundamental Right, its violation cannot be challenged directly under Article 32, but can be under Article 226.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions (Option 1): Wrong; it is no longer a fundamental right, and Article 300A does not guarantee compensation.

• It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process (Option 2): Wrong; deprivation must be by authority of a valid law.

• It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court (Option 4): Wrong; being a legal right, Article 32 is not directly available.

question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:
option_1: Proportional to its distance from the axis
option_3: Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis
solution_text:
The correct answer is The same for all particles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a rigid body (दृढ़ पिंड) rotating about a fixed axis, every particle sweeps the same angle in the same time.

• Therefore, the angular velocity (कोणीय वेग) is the same for all particles of the body.

• This is why angular velocity is treated as a property of the whole rotating body, not of individual particles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The linear velocity v = ωr does vary with distance r from the axis, being greater for particles farther out.

• Angular velocity ω is a vector directed along the axis of rotation (by the right-hand rule).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

NOTE

• Proportional to its distance from the axis (Option 1): True for linear velocity, not angular velocity.

• Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis (Option 3): Incorrect for both angular and linear velocity in a rigid body.

• Always zero (Option 4): Wrong; a rotating body has non-zero angular velocity.

question: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam(BSA) places emphasis on the use of technology to ensure the authenticity of evidence. This is particularly relevant for:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Digital and electronic evidence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम) replaced the colonial-era Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

• It gives special emphasis to digital and electronic evidence, treating electronic records as primary evidence and ensuring their authenticity.

• This reflects the modern need to handle emails, server logs, digital records and other electronic data in trials.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The BSA is one of the three new criminal laws effective from 1 July 2024, along with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

• It provides for authentication of electronic records, aligning with the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Physical exhibits from crime scenes (Option 1): Handled under evidence rules but not the special technological focus emphasised here.

• Hand-written diaries (Option 2): These are documentary evidence, not the electronic-authenticity focus.

• Oral confessions (Option 4): Oral evidence, unrelated to technology-based authenticity.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A) : The One Nation One Ration Card ensures portability of food grains.
Reason (R) : It uses Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) (एक राष्ट्र एक राशन कार्ड) scheme ensures portability of food grain entitlements across India — so Assertion (A) is true.

• It works through Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication at ePoS devices, which is exactly what makes portability possible — so Reason (R) is true and correctly explains A.

• Beneficiaries can lift their quota of subsidised grains from any Fair Price Shop anywhere in the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• ONORC is implemented under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, using the Integrated Management of PDS (IM-PDS) portal.

• It especially benefits migrant workers and their families.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): Wrong; biometric authentication is precisely why portability is achieved.

• A is true, but R is false (Option 3): Wrong; R is true.

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): Wrong; A is true.

question: Cheraw, the bamboo dance performed using crossed bamboo sticks, is a folk dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cheraw (चेराव), popularly called the bamboo dance, is the most famous folk dance of Mizoram (मिजोरम).

• Dancers step in and out of a grid of crossed bamboo sticks that are tapped rhythmically together.

• It is performed on festive and ceremonial occasions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other dances of Mizoram include Khuallam and Chheihlam.

• The main festivals of Mizoram are Chapchar Kut, Mim Kut and Pawl Kut.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• Meghalaya (Option 2): Known for dances like Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem.

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for the Bardo Chham and Ponung dances.

• Sikkim (Option 4): Known for the Singhi Chham (snow lion dance) and Maruni.

question: What is a key factor assessed in the Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Defense Budget.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Firepower (GFP) Military Strength Ranking (ग्लोबल फायरपावर रैंकिंग) evaluates the military potential of nations using a PowerIndex score.

• A key factor assessed is the Defense Budget (रक्षा बजट), along with manpower, equipment and geography.

• A lower PowerIndex value indicates a stronger, more capable military.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Over 60 individual factors are used, including active personnel, aircraft, tanks, naval assets, and natural resources.

• The USA, Russia and China consistently occupy the top three positions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Economic Stability (Option 1): While finance matters, the specific measured input is the defence budget, not general economic stability.

• Cultural Influence (Option 2): A soft-power concept, not a GFP military factor.

• Healthcare Spending (Option 3): Not a factor in the military strength index.

question: Which of the following correctly describes cooperative sector industries?
option_1: Owned and operated by central government agencies.
option_3: Owned by workers or suppliers sharing profits and losses
option_4: Maintained by foreign companies with Indian partnerships.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Owned by workers or suppliers sharing profits and losses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cooperative sector industries (सहकारी क्षेत्र के उद्योग) are owned and managed by the producers, workers or suppliers of raw materials.

• The members share the profits and losses collectively on the principle of mutual cooperation.

• A classic example is Amul (Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation), owned by dairy farmers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The economy is broadly divided into public, private, joint and cooperative sectors on the basis of ownership.

• Sugar mills in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh are common examples of the cooperative sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Owned and operated by central government agencies (Option 1): Describes the public sector, not the cooperative sector.

• Operated solely for export purposes (Option 2): Not a defining feature of cooperatives.

• Maintained by foreign companies with Indian partnerships (Option 4): Describes joint ventures/foreign collaboration, not cooperatives.

question: Education is now placed under which list after the 42nd Amendment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concurrent List.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (42वां संशोधन) shifted Education (शिक्षा) from the State List to the Concurrent List (समवर्ती सूची).

• This allowed both the Centre and the States to legislate on education.

• The amendment was enacted on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 42nd Amendment also transferred Forests, Protection of wild animals and birds, Weights and Measures, and Administration of Justice to the Concurrent List.

• It is often called the "Mini Constitution" because of the wide-ranging changes it introduced.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Union List (Option 1): Contains subjects on which only Parliament can legislate; education is not here.

• State List (Option 2): Education was here before 1976, but was moved out by the 42nd Amendment.

• Judicial List (Option 4): No such list exists in the Seventh Schedule.

question: What is the main objective of the National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS) launched in 2024?
option_3: To deliver sector-specific climate information services
option_4: To mandate carbon offsetting in the private sector
solution_text:
The correct answer is To deliver sector-specific climate information services.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS) (राष्ट्रीय जलवायु सेवा ढांचा) was launched in 2024 by the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

• Its main objective is to provide sector-specific climate information services (क्षेत्र-विशिष्ट जलवायु सूचना सेवाएं) to support informed decision-making.

• It focuses on key sectors such as agriculture, water, health, energy and disaster risk reduction.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is aligned with the WMO's Global Framework for Climate Services (GFCS).

• The NFCS was launched around the 150th anniversary/foundation events of the IMD.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• To set emission trading targets (Option 1): That relates to carbon markets, not climate services.

• To regulate groundwater quality (Option 2): A water-resource regulation task, not the NFCS objective.

• To mandate carbon offsetting in the private sector (Option 4): Not the purpose of NFCS.

question: Argon is produced in Earth's crust via?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decay of K-40.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Argon (आर्गन) in the Earth's crust is produced mainly by the radioactive decay of Potassium-40 (K-40).

• K-40 decays into Argon-40 (Ar-40) through electron capture, which accumulates over geological time.

• This is why Argon-40 is the most abundant argon isotope in the atmosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This decay is the basis of the Potassium-Argon (K-Ar) dating method used to date rocks.

• Argon is a noble gas and the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere (about 0.93%).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

NOTE

• Volcanoes (Option 2): Volcanoes release trapped gases but are not the source of argon's formation.

• Photosynthesis (Option 3): A biological process producing oxygen, unrelated to argon.

• Cosmic rays (Option 4): Produce certain isotopes but are not the main source of crustal argon.

question: Which of the following is true about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs?
option_1: Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
option_2: DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
option_3: Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
option_4: DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Rights (मौलिक अधिकार) in Part III are justiciable — they are legally enforceable in courts (Articles 32 and 226).

• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) (डीपीएसपी) in Part IV are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by any court (Article 37).

• However, DPSPs are fundamental in the governance of the country and the State must apply them in making laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Rights were inspired by the US Constitution, while DPSPs were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

• In Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court held that a balance between FRs and DPSPs is part of the basic structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

NOTE

• Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts (Option 1): Wrong; DPSPs are not justiciable.

• DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict (Option 2): Wrong; Fundamental Rights generally prevail (with limited exceptions like Article 31C).

• DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional (Option 4): Wrong; Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and enforceable, not optional.
